plugin.name: Fyrox (Rust)
plugin.description: Builds 2D and 3D games with Fyrox, the Rust game engine: a ready starter project, checking and running from a panel, and a Skill for the 1.0 API.
plugin.longDescription: Fyrox is a 2D and 3D game engine written in Rust, with its own scene, materials, physics and UI. The plugin creates a Rust project with the starter Fyrox scene, adds a panel to check and run the game, and gives the agent a Skill for the 1.0 API, scripts, scenes and the compile workflow. The panel lists every dependency (Rust, the C linker, Clippy, Fyroxed, the project manager) as essential or optional, checks what is installed, installs the safe Rust components, and links the official installer for the rest. The game opens in its own window, outside the OhMyGame preview.
type.title: Fyrox game (Rust)
type.description: A Rust project with Fyrox 1.0: starter 3D scene, executor and game plugin.
type.full.title: Fyrox complete (workspace)
type.full.description: The official project-manager layout: game, executor, integrated editor, hot reload, web and Android.
panel.title: Fyrox
ready.rust: Install Rust (rustup.rs) to build and run the game. The Fyrox panel shows the steps.
ready.linker: The C linker is missing: Build Tools on Windows, Xcode Command Line Tools on macOS, build-essential on Linux. See the Environment section in the Fyrox panel.
ready.rust_version: The installed Rust is older than the project needs. Run rustup update stable and try again.
command.install: Install a Fyrox dependency (from the panel)
command.setEditor: Set the Fyroxed executable (from the panel)
config.fyroxedPath.title: Fyroxed executable
config.fyroxedPath.description: Optional: the portable Fyroxed executable. The plugin checks that the file exists and shows its path in the Environment section; it does not launch the editor.
config.targetDir.title: Build folder (target)
config.targetDir.description: Optional: where cargo writes target/ (CARGO_TARGET_DIR). Use another drive, such as P:\caches\fyrox-target, to save space on C:. Empty uses the project's target/.
